subject: strategy
text: - **Command-line checks and shell flows (since 2026-10-10-driver-cli):** seven_guis' checks run the package's own `escher-session` binary once per command as a client process and read its stdout, its stderr and its exit status — `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error — through the shared runner of `tests/common/mod.rs`, which bounds the run and drains both streams; and two POSIX `sh` scripts under `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/` (`counter.sh`, `flight.sh`), a non-Rust test asset, are run under plain `sh` by the Rust target `cli_flow`, and since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay a third, `record_checks.sh` (the binary and an existing output directory its two arguments, `rec/` made `0700`, printing only `step N` on failure), by seven_guis `recording`'s unix-gated `the_committed_checks_are_what_the_binary_records` — the scripts are assets of a `cargo test` target, not a runner of their own, and no test framework is added; the three targets are `cfg(unix)`-gated (examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs:57-128; examples/seven_guis/tests/cli_flow.rs:31-74; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/report.md)

subject: strategy
text: - **Recorded-check replay (since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay):** a check a session recorded, committed as data under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` (`counter-cli.json`, `counter-mcp.json`, git mode `100644`), read by the strict `Check::from_bytes` and run as an ordinary `cargo test` target (`stand_replay`) through `Check::replay` — every step re-validated through `Session::run`, red at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs, the answers compared as JSON values — and kept fresh by a byte-for-byte comparison with what the binary records (seven_guis `recording`); picked up by `agent-run.sh run stand`, stand-repeat and the CI `test` leg on three OSes with no script change (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_replay.rs:24-36; examples/seven_guis/tests/recording.rs:187-203)

text: - **Claims mapped to checks:** `docs/capabilities.md`, a document with no runtime surface, ends on `## Where each claim is proven`, naming the check behind each claim it makes — the stand checks the `stand-repeat` leg runs among them — and states each limit as pinned by its check or as asserted by no check (the `select` model's limits); only its names and counts are held to the schema's tables, by the CI-script pin `test_capability_statement.py` (§4), so a check renamed or moved changes that section by hand (docs/capabilities.md:172-174; docs/capabilities.md:188-192; docs/capabilities.md:300-301)

text: - **blitz-test-harness:** `settle.rs` pins the load counter — an answered request reaches the inner handler with its url and bytes and leaves none in flight, a handler dropped unanswered leaves none, the finished count grows by one per handler and never falls, `is_noop` is the inner provider's — the settle loop — an idle document settles in one pass, work for k polls in k + 1, work for ever ends after exactly `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT` polls as `Render`, a request in flight after a quiet pass reads `Loads` after one poll, a handler finishing inside a pass costs one more pass, a wrapped HTML document is read through its render-blocking resources — and that every `NotSettled` message is non-empty, distinct and holds no `/` (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:193-462); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `screenshot.rs` pins the shot — the whole viewport painted at its device size, what the page leaves unpainted reading opaque white, a rectangle being that part of the frame, a rectangle past the viewport clipped and one outside it an error, a document with no font refused, and a shot the same twice (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:140-244); since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness `contrast.rs` pins the contrast reader — `contrast_ratio` as the WCAG 2.x ratio over a stated table of 5 rows (21.0 both ways, 1.0, 4.48 and 4.39 within 0.005), `required_ratio` over a stated table of 5 rows (3.0 for large text — at least 24 px, or 14 pt at weight 700 — else 4.5), each row count asserted, and three fixture tests: a button reads its own text and background, a translucent ancestor is composited over the page, and an element with no text reads `None` (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs:200-308)

- **escher-driver:** wire.rs pins the closed grammar at `v3` (`v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording, which added the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed` reply) — `hello`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, a third request, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` (kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte, the decoder strict), and the replies — the lifecycle's, `hello`'s carrying `idle_expiry_s`, and `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` — round-trip; another version of a known word is `refused version`, anything else (a request line over 16,384 bytes, bytes that are not text, 51 malformed rows) is `refused malformed`, a reply outside the protocol does not parse, and a line is read up to its terminator and no further, an over-long or unterminated one named; a byte that is not plain is written as its escape, a decoded call equals the call that was encoded, the widest call the schema admits fits the request bound, and an answer at its 1,048,576-byte bound is carried while one byte over is not (a lifecycle reply is bounded at 128 bytes, the widest `hello` measuring 122); session.rs pins the label rule (1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`), that an invalid label returns `InvalidLabel` without the boot closure running, and the session's record of ids — the ids read are held, a re-read id becomes the most recently read, and past the bound the one read longest ago is forgotten, on a record of a small stated bound; the bound counts ids, and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the record holds no id longer than a call can name — an id longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES` is not recorded (`the_record_holds_no_id_longer_than_a_call_can_name`); error.rs pins that every `SessionError` message — the `NotSettled` arm's three, one per `Busy` class, included
 — is a non-empty fixed string holding no `/`, that an exit code is not in it and that the `Io` arm adds only the kind's name — the arm is spelled "input or output", since "I/O" holds a `/`; refusal.rs pins the closed cause set — eight causes in a stated order (`fonts-unavailable` the eighth, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), each name, meaning and remedy a fixed text against a stated table, the remedies pairwise distinct and no `/` in any — and a refusal's printed form, which opens with its cause's name and ends with its remedy; schema_tests.rs (`schema::tests`) pins the verb table — twelve verbs in a stated order and three levels (`Level::Instance` · `Level::Session` · `Level::Tool`, `Level::name` reading `instance` · `session` · `tool`: the eight instance-level verbs, `screenshot` after `scroll` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `lint` after `screenshot`, then `start`, `status`, `stop`, then, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`), each with help, arguments and at least one result field, the lookup by exact name only (a name differing in case or padding finds nothing), each verb's argument and result shapes, the seven argument kinds with their bounds (the sixth, `ArgKind::Name`, 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`; the seventh, `ArgKind::Part`, a whole number 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000), the field kinds, ten since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot (the seventh, `FieldKind::Count`; then `Words` and `Entries`, since 2026-10-12-self-description, and `Png`), and the twelve key names, so that an argument or a field of a wait would fail it, and, since that chunk, the thirteen node keys named in order, each with its help (`differs` after `bounds`), and the four exit statuses in status order; error.rs pins, since that chunk, that each of the session errors — fifteen since 2026-10-19-session-recording
 — states a kind, a meaning and a remedy and that the state directory's message states its bound (94 bytes on Linux, 90 elsewhere); since 2026-10-19-session-recording recording_tests.rs (`recording::tests`, in `recording.rs` until 2026-10-19-test-splits) pins the FNV-1a 64 digest of the written answer, a recording's read-back, the masked `type` stand-in, the calls no record can spell left out, owner-only modes with no file replaced and no foreign temporary removed, a recording ending at its bound or on a failed write with its check removed, and `Check::from_bytes`'s strict grammar (40 refusal rows and 8 read rows, the record keeping its answer, a shot's without `png`, edge rows at both bounds); since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay replay.rs that a check replayed on a fresh session holds, that an acceptance flip and a changed answer each stop the replay naming their keys, that a shot holds at its size whatever its pixels and that a check of another app runs nothing (packages/escher-driver/src/replay.rs:141-318); session.rs that a recording directory open to others is refused with nothing written and that a recording that ends reads failed once, and since 2026-10-20-load-wait the load wait over a scripted settle — a load answered inside the bound ends the wait settled, one never answered ends it at the bound still `Loads`, a `render` or `layout` answer returns at once, and a quiet settle returns after one settle and sleeps none (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:307-369); schema_tests.rs that the `settled` help states `LOAD_WAIT`, whole seconds, that the five acting verbs carry it and that the wait ends before an answer read (packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs:152-164); mcp_tests.rs that each session a recording boot starts is kept as one check and that a call that ends the recording is answered `isError` as its session error;
 client.rs that `ok v3 recording-failed` reads as `SessionError::RecordingFailed`; off unix, a recording refused `Unsupported` — `recording::off_unix_tests`, in `recording_off_unix_tests.rs` since 2026-10-19-test-splits (packages/escher-driver/src/recording_tests.rs:1-538; packages/escher-driver/src/recording_off_unix_tests.rs:1-15; packages/escher-driver/src/mcp_tests.rs:632-734); describe.rs that the document holds `help`'s seven fields in order and every text in it is its tables'; mcp_tests.rs (`mcp::tests`) that `help` is answered by the server with or without a session and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, that a result holding an image is bounded by its whole written form and a shot is written as its image block then its text block; image.rs, since that chunk, the hand base64 against RFC 4648's test vectors and every sextet of the alphabet, and the PNG encoder — a PNG decodes to the pixels it was given and holds no time or text chunk, and pixels that do not fill the size write nothing (packages/escher-driver/src/image.rs:39-107); since 2026-10-19-visual-lint lint.rs that `Defect::ALL` names the six defects in order (`overlap` · `clipped` · `truncated` · `off-screen` · `zero-size` · `contrast`) and that findings come in document order, then `Defect::ALL` order (packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:542-620); command.rs pins that a verb is checked at its own level only — `validate` refuses a session-level verb as `unknown-verb` before its arguments are read, `validate_session` admits the three session commands and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`, refusing an argument to it as `malformed`, and refuses an instance-level verb — and `validate` — admitted calls at each bound's edge and on every key, unknown verbs, one malformed witness per rule per kind, the first-failure order, and the table and `Command` in agreement
 — with every assertion over a call carrying a row index only, so a failing log prints no argument value; each table is stated in its test and its row count asserted, and four mutation controls each turned its named test red (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema/evidence/controls.md); execute.rs pins the executor's key table — each of the schema's twelve keys stands for one keyboard key, pairwise distinct, the row count asserted — and the command span: its eight field names against the table the span's own macro emits, none an argument's name, and each busy class reading as its schema word; json.rs pins the written forms — a string with its escapes, a number as the shortest decimal and `null` when not finite, a node with the schema fields it has (a masked value as `MASKED_VALUE`), each outcome with its verb's fields in order, each refusal from its cause's fixed strings, each session error with its kind and its message and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, its remedy, each session answer, and, since that chunk, a changed node with `differs` after `bounds`; cli_tests.rs (`cli::tests`, in `cli.rs` until 2026-10-19-test-splits) pins the command line — a line read by its rules in order (61 rows), an argument that is not text as a usage error, each ending's streams and status, the usage line built from the verb table and the app names, and a line that is no command or is refused running nothing; client.rs pins that a call's reply reads as its answer or as a session error and that a call the schema refuses is answered without a session, and, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, that the answer's per-read bound is `wire::ANSWER_BOUND`, 30 s, an answer never sent ending as `SessionError::Timeout` at a shortened bound;
 eight mutation controls of 2026-10-10-driver-cli each read red under its mutation and green on the restored tree (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-driver-cli/evidence/controls.md); since that chunk a `call` and its answer cross the socket, and the schema is driven over it by `stand_session_lifecycle` (a call that runs, one that is refused, five raw lines outside the grammar and one wrong-version line through a live socket, each of the six refused with nothing run) and through the `escher-session` binary by seven_guis' `cli_commands` (14), `cli_flow` (2), `host_timer` (1) and `host_log`, while the fifteen `stand_act_*` files drive it in process through a `Session` (§5), where nine mutation controls of 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans — five on the driver's span and its check, four on the sink's span line — each turned a named test red, every one of that chunk's nine new tests red at least once (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/evidence/controls.md), where five mutation controls of the executor each turned a named check red (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/evidence/controls.md) and nine more — each of the three screen readings removed, the record never consulted, the page point taken without the viewport's scroll, the order of two causes swapped, the engine's walk of the nested boxes removed, `off-screen` read against the viewport alone, `in_view` answered true always — each turned its named check red and read green again on the restored tree (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-refusal-detection/evidence/controls.md); and eleven mutation controls of 2026-10-12-self-description each reddened its named test, all eleven restores sha-equal (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-self-description/evidence/controls.md), and three of 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot — the mask off, the crop rounded inward, the font check removed
 — each turned exactly its target cases red, each restore sha256-equal (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/evidence/controls.md) (packages/escher-driver/src/describe.rs:97-234; packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:305-738; packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:246-438; packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:226-352; packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:203-336; packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs:1-404; packages/escher-driver/src/command.rs:378-905; packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:583-646) — the three schema files as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema/report.md, the executor's at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/report.md, the record's test, the sixth verb and the nine further controls at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-refusal-detection/report.md, the span's two tests and its controls at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md

text: | Network | `LoadNet`, the load page's network stand-in, private to `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs` — a third hand-written network stand-in beside `HeldNet` and `LateNet`: `stand::boot_load` replaces its options' `net_provider` with `Some(Arc::new(LoadNet))` through `..options`, every other boot keeping `net_provider: None` (`the_stand_options_stay_offline`); each `fetch` answers the fixed sheet `LOADED_CSS` for `http://stand.test/load.css` from a thread of its own after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms); it does not override `is_noop`, so the harness counts its load — `the_load_page_click_leaves_a_load_in_flight` reads it in flight and `stand_load_page`'s click waits it out and shows the message; no `blitz_net`, print, env read, socket or listener | (examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:141-175; examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:308-329; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_load_page.rs:34-68) |

subject: mocking
text: | Time (seven_guis timer) | `TimerTicks`, provided in context by every headless-stand boot, replaces the timer's 100 ms `futures_timer::Delay`: each `deliver(n)` tick is one 0.1 s step capped at the duration, applied on the next pass — a `pump`, an input helper's own pump, or a settle (`Harness::settle`, `Session::act`, each acting verb of `Session::run`) — so a delivery made before an input helper is applied by that helper's pump and one made after it by nothing until a later pass; settle neither advances the timer nor waits on a tick not yet delivered; an undelivered source holds elapsed at 0.0 s; the driver moves that time by `advance`, which moves the session's clock — the harness's `VirtualClock`, the clock every harness-built document reads — by exactly `ms` inside one settled step, then hands `ms` to the step: `seven_guis::stand::timer_step(ticks)` is the step the Timer's session carries through `Session::with_time` — it returns nothing and delivers the whole 100 ms ticks (`TIMER_TICK_MS`) the asks hold, carrying the remainder below one tick across calls (250 then 250 → 2 then 3 ticks); `advanced_ms` is exactly `ms`, the clock's move (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), not what the Timer's counter gained — 60000 is reported while the elapsed display stops at its 15 s duration | (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:10-20; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:47-55; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_timer.rs:7-46; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs:35-76; examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:92-109; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_timer.rs:1-12; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/evidence/red-first.md, the driver's `advance` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/report.md, on the one clock at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock/report.md) |
